basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 14.' and it opens 'Vers. 14. Locutus est ad generos suos. Quidam putant Lot habuisse filias quae viros'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 14. Locutus est ad generos suos. Quidam putant Lot habuisse filias quae viros haberent quos appellavit generos, et illas cum maritis in Sodomis remansisse, duabus aliis quae sine maritis erant cum patre egressis. Sed alia translatio dicit aperte: Locutus est ad sponsos qui accepturi erant filias. Ergo nondum | erant generi, sed esse volebant.
